title: Transport statistics in asymmetric coupled chaotic dots in series: Brownian motion model
authors: Ashutosh Dheer, Santosh Kumar, Jayendra N. Bandyopadhyay
abstract: We study statistics of transport properties in a system of two quantum chaotic cavities coupled in series through a tunable junction and connected to reservoirs with asymmetric leads. Within the random matrix theory framework and in the absence of time-reversal symmetry, the scattering matrix S undergoes a crossover from two independent circular unitary ensembles to a single CUE as the inter-cavity coupling increases. Modeling this crossover using Dyson's Brownian motion approach, with the junction width acting as a time-like parameter, we derive closed-form expressions for the time-dependent averages and variances of conductance and shot noise power for arbitrary lead asymmetry. These analytical results reduce to known expressions in the symmetric and fully coupled limits. The mapping between the Brownian time parameter and the physical junction width is found to be observable-dependent, reflecting the different eigenfunction correlations probed by conductance and shot noise power, and this dependence is examined and separately calibrated for each observable. Validating against random-matrix simulations and tight-binding transport calculations using Kwant, we find quantitative agreement for ensemble-averaged observables throughout the crossover, while variances, being more sensitive to microscopic fluctuations, show deviations from the Brownian-motion predictions.
summary: This paper analyzes the transport statistics in two coupled chaotic quantum cavities exhibiting a crossover in their underlying random matrix statistics. Using Dyson's Brownian motion model, the authors derive analytical formulas for conductance and shot noise, successfully reproducing ensemble averages across the crossover regime. The work highlights the limitations of the model when calculating variances, suggesting sensitivity to microscopic fluctuations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the statistics of transport properties, specifically conductance and shot noise, in a quantum system composed of two chaotic cavities coupled in series.
main_result: Closed-form analytical expressions for the time-dependent averages and variances of conductance and shot noise are derived, showing quantitative agreement with simulations for averages but deviations for variances.
method: The study employs Random Matrix Theory (RMT) and models the system's evolution using Dyson's Brownian motion approach, treating the junction width as a time-like parameter.
model_or_system: The system consists of two chaotic quantum cavities coupled via a tunable junction and connected to reservoirs with asymmetric leads. The underlying mathematical framework involves the crossover of the scattering matrix statistics from two independent Circular Unitary Ensembles (2CUE) to a single CUE.

why_interesting: The application of advanced RMT techniques like Dyson's Brownian motion to model transport crossovers in mesoscopic systems provides deep insights into how system connectivity affects quantum transport statistics, which is relevant to open quantum systems.
